SECTION ONE
Purpose, Scope, and Definitions
Purpose
ARTICLE 1. – (1) This directive regulates the procedures and principles regarding the storage of scientific and
intellectual studies of Gebze Technical University in the Gebze Technical University Academic Archive and making
them available to the scientific world through the Open Access System.
(2) The objectives of this directive are to ensure the long -term compilation and preservation of academic studies
produced by members of Gebze Technical University, to enhance the visibility of this scientific and intellectual
repository through open access, to establish the Gebze Technical University Academic Archive, to define the Open
Access strategy, and to organi ze this system in compliance with the "Open Archives Initiative Protocol for Metadata
Harvesting" (OAI-PMH) standards.
Scope
ARTICLE 2. – (1) This directive covers the provisions regarding the storage and open access of academic studies
supported directly or indirectly by Gebze Technical University and carried out by its members, in the Gebze Technical
University Academic Archive under the coordination of the Directorate of Library and Documentation.
(2) Materials constituting the content of Gebze Techni cal University Academic Archive include articles, master's and
doctoral theses, conference proceedings, seminar texts, technical notes, project result reports, books, chapters in books,
award-winning studies, patent documents, course materials, and multimedia materials.
Basis
ARTICLE 3. (1) This Directive has been prepared based on the provisions of Articles 4/c and 42/d of the Higher
Education Law No. 2547 and the Open Archives Initiative Protocol for Metadata Harvesting.
Definitions
ARTICLE 4. – (1) In this regulation, the following terms have the following definitions:
• Open Peer Review: A scientific review mechanism in which both the reviewer and the author have information
about each other's identities throughout the review and publication period
• Open Science: Science, publications, research data, laboratory notes, and other research processes that are made
freely accessible under conditions that allow the reuse, distribution, and production of the research in a way that
other researchers can collaborate and contribute
• Open Access: Scientific literature that can be accessed, read, saved, copied, printed, scanned, linked to the full
text, indexed, transferred to software as data and used for all kinds of legal purposes via the internet without
financial, legal and technical barriers
- Golden Open Access: The studies of researchers published in academic journals are open access through the
published journal and from the moment they are published
- Green Open Access: One copy of the accepted version of researchers' studies published in academic journals
is open access in open archives
• Open Education Resources: Teaching, learning, and research materials using open licenses that allow free reuse
and continuous improvement by others for educational purposes, according to the OECD
• Open Access System: An academic archive system that provides open access to academic and scientific outputs
produced by Gebze Technical University members, collected digitally, stored, indexed , and preserved for the
long term
• Open Data: Data that can be used, reused , and distributed free of charge and freely by anyone without being
subject to any copyright, patent, or other control mechanisms

• Academic Archive: Systems that collect, organize , and archive long -term publications, data , and other
intellectual products (theses, course materials, study reports, etc.) produced from scientific research supported
by public resources
• Academic Archive System: An archive that provides open access to the publications and research data of Gebze
Technical University researchers and is stored through Gebze Technical University Academic Archive software
• Academic Study: All studies resulting from the research, funds received , and creative activities of Geb ze
Technical University Members
• Embargoed: Academic studies and research results that are closed to certain access for various reasons (patent
application, book publishing, institutional reasons, etc.)
• Research: Any creative and systematic study with the aim of advancing knowledge
• Researcher: Any member of Gebze Technical University research staff at all levels, including employees and
doctoral students, regardless of their level of employment
• Research Data: Data used to verify the results presented in scientific publications (e.g. statistics, experimental
results, measurements, observations, interview records, images, etc.) or other data used during a project and
described in the Data Management Plan
• Archiving: Process of storing the academic studies to which Gebze Technical University members contribute
scientifically and intellectually in the academic archive in a way that can be made available for open access
• European Open Science Cloud Cloud -EOSC: The details of which were announced by the European
Commission in April 2018, it is the collection of "embedded" data of 1.7 million researchers and 70 million
science and technology experts in the European Union in academic journals and books, making this data
available to everyone
• Storage: All of the actions that must be taken to ensure continuous access to digital materials when necessary
• DOI (Digital Object Identifier ): Identifiers that describe an intellectual property or a part of this intelle ctual
property available online
• FAIR Principles: An acronym for research data management or any of the initiatives related to the European
Open Science Cloud. It is based on the pr inciples of data being Findable, Accessible , Interoperable , and
Reusable
• Gebze Technical University Member: Gebze Technical University staff and students
• OpenAIRE: A technical open access infrastructure project that enables access to scientific publication outputs,
open research data, and research information, analysis of data and provides various services to content providers
in line with the European Commission's open science goals
• ORCID (Open Researcher and Contributor ID): The alphanumeric code used to uniquely identify scientists and
academic authorities
• Copyright: All the material and moral rights that a person has legally over the products he /she produces with
all his intellectual efforts
• Compliant Archive: An archive that meets quality standards such as FAIR Principles, OpenAIRE compliance,
and CoreTrust Seal certification)
• University: Gebze Technical University
• Metadata: A set of data that describes an information source; in other words, structured, descriptive information
about the discovery, identification, use, and management of digital information and information resources
• Data Management Plan: A tool that shows how researchers will meet their responsibilities regarding research
data quality, data sharing, and data security
• Publication: Peer-reviewed published (or being published) studies of researchers in the institution

Policy

ARTICLE 5. – (1) The University aims to contribute to the advancement of science and technology by adopting clear,
reproducible and reliable research outputs and applications. It is committed to the broad dissemination of knowledge to
the benefit of society and all its external stakeholders.
(2) The University accepts " openness" as one of its guiding principles and, in addition to this principle, is open to
publications and data that enable new working models and new social relations, enabling collaboration, dissemination
of knowledge, accessibility and reusability of research outputs. It is committed to developing and encouraging tools and
research processes that promote access and build the infrastructure necessary to support open science.
(3) Open science makes research more trans parent, rigorous, and efficient. It encourages innovation and public
participation. The University believes that all publicly-funded research and research data should be made freely available
to the public and all researchers around the world.
(4) The directive is valid for all researchers active at the University. Where research is funded by third parties, any
agreements with parties regarding access rights, storage, and retention take precedence over this directive.
Open Access to Publications
ARTICLE 6. – (1) Requires researchers to place in the academic archive the full text (published article or peer-reviewed
copy of the article before publication) as well as a machine-readable electronic copy of the relevant metadata before or
after publication. Researchers are responsible for ensuring that their publications are put in the academic archive in a
timely manner. This also applies if publications are published in open access (Gold Open Access).
(2) In the case of “Green Open Access”, the University requires that the full texts of all publications be made available
under a standard open license within a maximum of 6 months (or within 12 months for publications in the social sciences
and humanities ). Monographs must be put in the academic archive, but access remains closed until the publisher
embargo ends.
(3) In order to increase the visi bility of “closed-access” publications, the metadata of the publication must be openly
accessible.
(4) University Members can store the studies they have prepared in collaboration with more than one author from more
than one institution in the Gebze Technical University Academic Archive. In multi -author studies carried out by more
than one Gebze Technical University Member, the lead author stores the source.
(5) When evaluating the publications of its members individually or institutionally, the University evaluates only
publications whose metadata and full texts are placed in the academic archive in accordance with the above-mentioned
conditions.
(6) The University encourages its members to protect copyright ownership and to license to publishers only the rights
necessary for publication.
(7) The University encourages researchers to place publications they have made before the effective date of this directive
in the academic archive and to make these publications openly accessible as soon as possible.
Open Access to Research Data
ARTICLE 7. – (1) The University requires researchers to place the research data necessary to verify the results
presented in scientific publications in an archive appropriate to international standards.
(2) The University requires that data and services be open and treated according to FAIR principles. Data should also
be traceable and available wherever possible.
(3) The University adheres to the Research Ecosystem principle of "as open as possible, as closed as necessary". If data
is not available for legal, privacy or other relevant reasons (e.g. sensitive data or personal data), this must be explained
clearly. In all cases, it provides metadata that enables the data to be found.
(4) The University encourages the adoption of Open Science Cloud terms for monitoring Open Science resources.
(5) The University provides researchers with an appropriate Data Management Plan for each research activity in which
they are involved.
(6) University researchers define post-project usage rights by determining appropriate licenses.
(7) The minimum archive period for university research data is 10 years after the assignment of a permanent identifier.
If these records are deleted or destroyed after the required archive period has expired or for legal and ethical reasons,
all legal and ethical perspectives of such actions need to be taken into account.

Open Science
ARTICLE 8. – (1) The University actively promotes the understanding of Open Science applications. For example, it
tracks participation in citizen science projects, use of open peer review, use of open educational resources, release of
data and content under open and standard open licenses, and their progress.
Infrastructure
ARTICLE 9. (1) The University meets the quality sta ndards approved by the OpenAIRE -compliant FAIR principles
and is connected to the European Open Science Cloud.
(2) The University ensures that records are interoperable with archives complying with international standards and
through the OpenAIRE Metadata Schema.
SECTION THREE
Authority and Responsibilities
Academic Archive and Open Access Commission
ARTICLE 10. (1) Gebze Technical University Rectorate pioneers the establishment of the Academic Archive and Open
Access Commission and undertakes the execution of this Commission.
(2) Members of the Academic Archive and Open Access Commission are appointed by the University S enate for a
period of three years upon the recommendation of the Rector, and may be reappointed or replaced by the Senate when
deemed necessary. The Commission consists of Faculty Deans or Vice-Rectors, Institute Directors or Deputy Directors,
the representative of the Directorate of Information Technology, the Director of Library and Documentation , and
representatives of appropriate divisions, under the chairpersonship of the Rector or Vice-Rector. The secretariat of the
Commission is carried out by the Directorate of Library and Documentation.
(3) With the recommendation of the Academic Archive and Open Access Commission and the approval of the Rector,
a Data Manager is designated to be responsible for all matters related to data in compliance with National and European
Union laws, including but not limited to issues related to the development of Data Management Plans.
(4) The Academic Archive and Open Access Commission will be responsible for evaluating the directive and planning
the implementation process every year after this directive enters into force. The Commission is responsible for revising
the directive when deemed necessary. It explores appropriate financing opportunities for these activities and
collaboration with other stakeholders.
(5) The Academic Archive and Open Access Commission follows the work of the European Open Science Policy
Platform and encourages the development of a research evaluation framework that promotes research quality and Open
Science behavior and practices, and the establishment of award mechanisms for researchers. It monitors the content of
the academic archive with statistics provided by the system and monitors directive compliance.
Directorate of Library and Documentation
ARTICLE 11. (1) According to Article 4/c of the Higher Education Law No. 2547, universities are responsible for
conducting high -level research and disseminating the results to become distinguished members of the scientific
community. Under Article 42/d, they are also responsible for comprehensively compiling the institution's scientific and
intellectual output. Within this framework, the Directorate of Library and Documentation is responsible for fulfilling
this requirement through the Gebze Technical University Academic Archive Open Access System initiative.
(2) It checks the records of scientific studies transferred to the system by Gebze Technical University members according
to the Open Archives Initiative Protocol for Metadata Harvesting (OAI-PMH) standards. When necessary, it collaborates
with the members of Gebze Technical University to make corrections and enforces the use of unique identifiers ( such
as DOIs, ORCID, or others).

(3) Monitors the content of the academic archive with statistics provided by the system, and monitors directive
compliance in coordination with other divisions. Before full-text publications are opened in the Academic Archive Open
Access System, all copyright permissions are checked against the SHERPA/Romeo database by library staff.
(4) The University Library Directorate, in collaboration with departments and other appropriate institutions (such legal
services, research support staff, Data Management Plan experts), provides training courses to facilitate the adoption of
open science and provide the necessary skills and expertise to researchers, librarians, and other support staff. Coordinates
the opening of s uch training courses that include the necessary skills for open access publishing, open data, data
management, research data, and research ethics. Training is offered to researchers at all career stages, taking into account
different disciplines, and is included in the curriculum.
(5) Ensures that the institution's academic archives and other research infrastructures comply with the certification
requirements r egarding FAIR data principles (Findable, Accessible , Interope rable, Reusable ) and European Open
Science Cloud technical specifications. It follows an Open License policy to publish content and data.
Directorate of Information Technology
ARTICLE 12. (1) The Directorate of Information Technology carries out the processes of installing, updating,
maintaining, backing up, protecting, and storing the Academic Archive and Open Access System software, ensuring its
security, and transferring data to the National Academic Archive system in accordance with open access standards. It
also provides mechanisms and services for appropriate guidance to researchers.
Gebze Technical University Members
ARTICLE 13. (1) Members of Gebze Technical University record the scientific and intellectual studies they produce
during their employment at the university, by making transactions via the internet, within the framework of legal
conditions, to be published in the Gebze Technical University Academic Archive and Open Access System.
(2) Members of Gebze Technical University agree that their scientific and intellectual contributions will be stored in the
Gebze Technical University Academic Archive and made available for Open Access, and that they will be archived in
accordance with the principles of public distribution and preservation.
(3) Members of Gebze Technical University app rove the pre-print, final print, or publisher's edition of their academic
studies, to which they have made scientific and intellectual contributions, to be stored in the Gebze Technical University
Academic Archive and made available for open access, in line with the conditions permitted by the publisher.
(4) Members of Gebze Technical University approve the storage of the latest versions of their academic studies in
accordance with the conditions permitted by the publisher, unless it is limited or completely blocked due to embargo or
similar conditions.
(5) Members of Gebze Technical University approve the storage of their scientific studies carried out during the current
year in the Gebze Technical University Academic Archive and Open Access System until the end of that academic year
at the latest, within the framework of legal conditions and in a way that does not violate the terms of agreements made
with publishers. Studies for which a patent application is planned can be stored on the same date as the patent publication
after the application is made.
(6) Free access to the full texts of studies in Gebze Technical University Academic Archive and Open Access System
depends on the author's decision and the copyright status of the publication.
(7) Resources to be included in the Academic Archive can be added to the system at any time of the year. However,
these added resources are not made available for open access until the date they will be published in the journal or until
the end of the “embargo” period determined by the publisher/author.
(8) Gebze Technical University supports its members who wish to have their research published with the "open access"
option. Considering the agreements made by the authors with the publishers and the storage options, access to the studies
is implemented under the titles "public access" and "open access after the embargo period".
(9) In multi -author studies carried out by more than one Gebze Technical University member, the responsibility for
storing the source belongs to the lead author who is a member of the university.

Enforcement
ARTICLE 14. (1) This directive will enter into force as of the date it is approved by the University Senate. It is reviewed
and updated every three years. The part of this directive related to research data is implemented on a pilot basis for three
years from the date of entry into force of this directive.
Execution
ARTICLE 15. (1) Gebze Technical University Rectorate assumes the executive role in the implementation of this
directive, in resolving any disputes that may arise, and in any changes that may be made to the policy.
